title: Toronto Newar Summer School 2027: free online courses in modern and classical Newar
dek: The University of Toronto's Centre for Buddhist Studies will teach Newar online from 12 April to 1 May 2027, with courses for beginners and advanced students. Applications by email close on 28 February 2027.
body: The Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Centre for Buddhist Studies, in the University of Toronto's Department for the Study of Religion, will hold its Toronto Newar Summer School online from 12 April to 1 May 2027. The announcement, posted on the INDOLOGY mailing list by Christoph Emmrich on 14 November 2026, says participation is free.

The school offers three modules and seven courses: two beginners' courses in modern conversational Newar, beginners' and advanced courses in modern literary Newar and in classical Newar, and a tutorial combining conversational and literary Newar. Classes of one to two hours meet six days a week, Monday to Saturday, for two weeks within a three-week period. Most courses run from 12 to 24 April; the advanced course in modern literary Newar runs from 19 April to 1 May. Guest lectures on Newar language, literature and religion are also planned.

The teachers named are Srilaxmi Shrestha and Geeta Manandhar for conversational Newar, Christoph Emmrich for literary and classical Newar, Bal Gopal Shrestha for the advanced literary course and Ian Turner for the combined conversational and literary tutorial.

The announcement says the school caters for beginners as well as intermediate and advanced students. To join, applicants email Christoph Emmrich by 28 February 2027 describing their interests, their educational, professional and language background, and the courses they wish to take. The contact address is given in the list announcement.
